text:
Shawn Park: heads-up — spotted a weird pattern after last night's AZ failover. fallback routing moved ~12 ongoing allocations into dedicated-pool-apac but ~6 of them show as RESERVED and never actually bound to a task. capacity looks fragmented and tail latency spiked for a handful of tenants.

ops-bot: [alert] 2024-11-03T02:14:12Z egress-policer: route-fallback -> dedicated-pool-apac (reason=az-telemetry-loss) allocations=12 reserved=12 bound=6

Lina Gomez: ugh, so the router reserved slots but the node agent never accepted the container? any node drains or preemptions in that window?

Shawn Park: checking. kube-events show a sequence of drain+preempt for a preemptible slab, but the scheduler still marked the new slots as "reserved" before we completed the handoff. logs attached:
```
I1103 02:14:14 scheduler.go:412] Reserve(tenant=tenant-ark, pool=dedicated-apac, id=alloc-7f8a) -> reserved
I1103 02:14:15 router.go:289] dispatch(alloc-7f8a) -> node-11 (acked)
I1103 02:14:16 node-agent.go:78] bind(alloc-7f8a) failed: timeout waiting for container runtime
```

Carl E: container runtime timeouts on edge nodes have been flakey since the nightly kernel patch. we saw similar but not-reserved behavior earlier. two options: (1) make router wait for node-agent bind ACK before marking reserved; (2) mark reserved but set short TTL so ghost-reservations auto-release.

Zoe M: cost and perf impact? reserved but unbound slots reduce usable pool size -> customers hit soft-cap and get routed to higher-cost fallback region or have their requests deferred. saw ~4% cost bump for one tenant during the spike.

Lina Gomez: option 1 reduces ghosting but increases routing latency (needs synchronous ack). option 2 is simpler and low-risk. we could set TTL=30s and observe. what about race with preemptions? if node-agent later binds after TTL we risk double-bind.

Shawn Park: plan: implement TTL-based guard for now + metric for "reserved-not-bound-duration". If we see many binds after TTL, escalate to Ack-based flow. I'll open a short-lived probe feature: set TTL=25s and instrument.

Carl E: add a histogram for reserved->bound latency and a counter for binds-after-ttl. also add an emergency reclaim that converts RESERVED->EVICT if no bind and node shows high drain activity.

ops-bot: [deploy] canary: router/alloc-reserve-ttl=25s -> rollout started to 5% of apac routing, tags: canary/ttl-25s

Zoe M: please tag affected customers so support can message if there are ongoing latency hits. I can correlate billing spikes.

Shawn Park: @Lina can you add a quick alert: reserved_unbound_count > 3 over 5m in a single AZ -> pager? we want ops in the loop before big fragmentation.

Lina Gomez: will do. setting alert and dashboard panel under "alloc-reserve". also adding a log query to find examples: `kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide | grep Reserved`

Carl E: follow-up: schedule kernel rollback window for the edge nodes we patched last night, and throttle router canary to avoid mass re-reserves during the rollback.

Shawn Park: thanks all. I'll follow up with the canary results in ~30m and create a postmortem if this repeats. short action list: TTL canary, metrics+alert, support tagging, node rollback window. :thumbsup:
